> == Would the boot cases catch regressions? Yes. Planted, booted, reverted ==
> - ipd lets labelled callers in: d3-net-attacks FAILS with '[net-rig] FAIL: buckets: two more accounts held, a third refused ([true, false, false])'.
> - ipd without the self-set check: d3-net-attacks FAILS.
> - ipd with the scope check removed: d3-net-attacks FAILS (the peer outside the prefix is reached).

> 
> == Trusted verdicts ==
> Every attack verdict comes from the rig (exit codes, the victim's reports, the bucket count), the bench's helper records, or the pcap. Clients are launched with only their `net` and `rig` handles and no console, so an attacker can't print `[net-rig]` lines. The attack lines' text after the colon is information only: what reached the network is judged outside the guest.
> P3-1: the labelled client's own `not refused 0x0` report is from the attacker. It is backed by trusted checks (the bucket count caught the planted regression), but mark it informational.
> P3-2: the labelled client's connect attempt writes the connect op to its `clone` fid (Socket { ctl: CLONE, data: CLONE }). Even if ipd let a labelled caller through, it would send no SYN, so 'its peer 10.0.9.112 counts 0' is vacuous evidence; the case catches the regression only through buckets and the refusal bits. Make it walk tcp/N/ctl when the clone read succeeded.
> 
> == The peer and the capture (peer.rs) ==
> - **Helper:** one process per guest connection (guestfwd cmd:). It records with create_new and a pid+random name, retrying on collision, before echoing, and closes without echoing if it can't record. count_records refuses any stray name. Exact counts both ways (records and capture SYN source ports), a 2 s settle, and records for a non-peer fail.
> - **pcap parse, fail-closed:** a missing, empty, short-header, cut (captured != length or > snaplen), trailing, foreign-magic or foreign-linktype file all fail, as does one with no frames.
> - **inspect:** only frames whose source is slirp's MAC are skipped (any other is treated as the guest's). ARP must be a request for the gateway, or a reply. IPv4 must be well-formed, unfragmented TCP. A SYN without ACK to self_forbidden fails.
> - **check_net:** peers are distinct, inside the /16 and outside slirp's /24; there is a positive control (connections > 0); self_forbidden needs peers.
> - **Ties to the rig:** a host test ties the cases' self_forbidden to the rig's SELF_ARGS plus ipd's fixed list, and there is a restrict=on test for every [net] case, the /16 included.
> P3-3: a frame from the SUT carrying slirp's source MAC would go unjudged. Only netd and ipd emit, and smoltcp uses its own MAC, so this is acceptable; state it.
> 
> == The /16 layout ==
> The self-set story is unchanged. The milestone keeps slirp's /24 with self=10.0.2.0/24, and peer cases put peers at 10.0.9.x, which only restrict=on makes safe (tested).
> 
> == Review-5 fixes, all verified and each caught when planted ==
> - **8b1004921:** classify runs the martian test before the protocol test and drops every non-TCP IPv4. The planted reordering is caught by `non_tcp_and_martian_datagrams_get_no_answer`.
> - **7350777ed:** my earlier survivors are now caught: any-badge frames and labelled-ingress frames (`frames_count_only_from_the_unlabelled_ingress_badge`), ephemeral duplicates (`a_port_in_use_is_drawn_again`), and the grant undo (`a_grant_nobody_received_is_undone`).
> - **3d8743617:** sockets are State units reserved per request from the caller's bucket and share (at most 8), made only from that reservation (Meter::Closed outside requests), and given back only when smoltcp has removed the socket, so a bucket stays held while its sockets linger. Planted bugs caught: no reservation (`a_listener_accepts_through_ctl`), units never returned (`a_lingering_socket_keeps_its_bucket`), and every badge sharing one share (`an_agent_cannot_take_all_its_sponsors_sockets`).
> - **Worst-case bound:** each override slot counts max(state + sockets, the default's), plus the rest at the default. Milestone: sshd 0+20 = 20, steward 32+0 = 32, default 4+8 = 12, 6 buckets: 20 + 32 + 4 x 12 = **100**. fits() costs every unit as a socket, so the memory bound holds.
> - **37da26e0c:** u64 scope ids, and the ARP-per-SYN residual stated.
> - **5f4ae6441:** netd drains until the used ring is empty before every IRQ wait, so a lost edge can't strand frames. Under a flood it loops without waiting, which is paced by ipd's 50 ms send and covered by the stated netd CPU residual.
> - **Provenance (40af0efc1, 3d5093263):** with the table header renamed it now says 'no vendored table' and exits 1, where it used to pass; the normal run is all ok.
> 
> == Deviations ==
> - **net-client, one program with roles:** fine; the rig chooses the role.
> - **Rig root limits 4:5:8:8:** fine.
> - **The labelled budget from SYSTEM:** acceptable, because ipd's check doesn't depend on class, but the rig's comment misreads KERNEL-SPEC. budget_create requires the *caller's* budget to be system-class to add labels, not the parent's. The rig is system-class, so it should be able to make a user-class labelled child under USERS, which is the production shape. Try that (P3-4); if the kernel refuses, raise a spec/kernel mismatch.
> - **INTERIM 1 ms ticks before K5:** acceptable, and remove them with K5.
>

It didn't reproduce in four clean runs, and no orphan remained, so I take it as my harness, not the code.
